newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX jittery ahead of holiday, French poll.
newsitem.headline: German DAX jittery ahead of holiday, French poll.

text.p: German shares peaked and troughed over the course of electronic trade on Wednesday, hitting record highs before tumbling over one percent in a jittery session ahead a regional holiday in Germany.

The German equity market became even more paranoid after the French stock market dropped four percent on rumours that polls showed the opposition Socialists were well placed for Sunday's run-off parliamentary elections.
By 1327 GMT the IBIS DAX index had recovered its composure somewhat and stood at 3,545.86 points, down 19.57 points or 0.53 percent.

Many market players were unwilling to take new positions ahead of Corpus Christi, which is a market and public holiday in the states of Baden-Wuerttemberg, Bavaria, Hesse, North Rhine-Westphalia, Rhineland Palatinate, Saarland, Saxony (partly) and Thuringia.

"The weakness today is mostly due to the Corpus Christi regional holiday tomorrow, because a lot of people will take Friday off and turn it into a long weekend. Also everyone is nervous ahead of the French elections," a trader said.
The markets would read a victory for the left in France as negative for EMU stability, the trader said.
Others said that market had come off late in the session after it found itself unable to penetrate the 3,700-point threshold, viewed as psychologically important in keeping market sentiment buoyant.
Among the main features on the market was Daimler-Benz AG, which forecast a rise in sales and earnings in full-year 1997, while sales in the first four months rose 15 percent to 36.3 million marks.
The shares rose to a high of 136.45 marks early on, but despite the upbeat figures, fell back 1.85 marks to to 134.25 marks in afternoon trade.
"It is increasingly the case that it is better to travel than arrive with the stock market the way it is at the moment," a trader said.
"Daimler was in line, but everyone is looking for something special, a little bit extra, in the current climate," he said.
Another big mover over the day was BMW which was down 4.16 percent at 1,425 marks in afternoon trade, having earlier gone as high as 1,510 marks.
Dealers said that the stock has become quite volatile of late, and that today's performance bore out that view.
Volkswagen was also lower, and dealers said it could be down to a run of profit-taking on dollar-led stocks.

Insurance giant Allianz was also down. Shares rose over 1.20 percent to 385.50 marks, but fell over the day and were down 6.20 marks at 372.80 marks in late trade, which traders also said was due to profit-taking.
